summary: Defines a SIP event package for registrations. Registrations are state in the network that can change, for example when administrators alter them, and this lets a user agent be notified when that state changes. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines a SIP event package called reg for updates about registrations. A subscriber receives information when the contacts linked to an address-of-record change.

questions: how to get notified when sip registration changes
what is the sip reg event package
how do i get notified when a sip registration changes
what is an address-of-record in sip
subtitle: SIP subscribers can receive updates when contacts registered to an address-of-record change.

tldr.problem: SIP registrations change when contacts are added, removed, refreshed, expire, or are changed by an administrator. Other applications may need to learn about those changes.
tldr.mechanism: The reg event package uses SIP SUBSCRIBE and NOTIFY. Notifications carry XML describing full registration state or the contacts that changed.
tldr.outcome: Subscribers can track registration state, but the information can be private and needs access controls. RFC 3680 is updated by RFC 6140.

facts.label: Recommended notification interval
facts.value: No faster than once every 5 seconds per subscriber

today: RFC 3680 is a Proposed Standard, published in March 2004, and is updated by RFC 6140. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Registrations Are Changing Network State
sections.content:
A SIP registration binds an address-of-record to one or more contact URIs. A proxy uses those contacts to forward or redirect requests for the address-of-record. The REGISTER method can add, remove, or query contacts.

Registrations can also change because an administrator changes policy or because a contact expires without being refreshed. The SIP Events framework provides SUBSCRIBE and NOTIFY; RFC 3680 defines a package for following registration changes.
sections.plainLanguage: A registration records where a SIP user can be reached. This event package lets a subscriber learn when that record changes.

sections.title: Examples of Registration Notifications
sections.content:
The RFC describes three possible uses. A device can subscribe to its registration so an administrator can shorten the registration and prompt the device to authenticate again. A presence server can use registration state as one input when it builds a presence document.

An application can also subscribe to learn when a user's device registers, then send a SIP MESSAGE to that device. These are example uses of the package, not additional protocol requirements.
sections.plainLanguage: A device can learn when it needs to register again, and a presence service can use registration changes as input. An application can also learn when a device registers and send it a message.

sections.title: The reg Event Package
sections.content:
The package name is reg, carried in the Event header of SUBSCRIBE and NOTIFY requests. A SUBSCRIBE may contain a filter body, but this RFC does not define its format. Without a body, the default policy sends a notification for each contact change and includes the changed contacts.

A notification caused by SUBSCRIBE contains the full list of contacts. The default registration expiration is 3600 seconds, and the default subscription duration is 3761 seconds. A different subscription duration can be requested with Expires.
sections.plainLanguage: A subscriber uses the name reg when it asks for updates. By default, notices list changed contacts, while a new subscription receives the full list.

sections.title: Registration and Contact States
sections.content:
Each address-of-record has registration states named init, active, and terminated. It begins in init, becomes active when its first contact is registered, and becomes terminated when its last contact is removed or expires. It then returns immediately to init; that final transition MUST NOT be reported in a NOTIFY.

Each contact has its own state machine. It can become active through a REGISTER or another creation process; while active, it can be refreshed or shortened. It can terminate as expired, deactivated, probation, unregistered, or rejected. Notification policy determines which transitions are reported, subject to the stated restriction.
sections.plainLanguage: An address-of-record has a state that shows whether any contacts are registered. Each contact also has a state and a reason for its latest change.

sections.title: Registration Information Documents
sections.content:
NOTIFY bodies use application/reginfo+xml, encoded as UTF-8 and using the namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:reginfo. The root element includes a version and a state value of full or partial. Registration elements identify an address-of-record and contain contact elements with state and event information.

A subscriber keeps its own tables from the documents. Full state replaces the stored tables; partial state updates them. If the version jumps by more than one, the subscriber processes the document and SHOULD request a refresh to obtain full state. Older versions are discarded.
sections.plainLanguage: Each notification has a version and says whether it contains all registration data or only changes. The subscriber uses those fields to replace or update its saved view.

sections.title: Protecting Registration Information
sections.content:
Registration information can be sensitive and private. Subscriptions SHOULD be authenticated and authorized according to local policy. The RFC also recommends protecting notifications for confidentiality, integrity, and verification of the subscriber's identity.

It gives SIPS URLs and S/MIME protection of notification bodies as examples. The security considerations for the SIP Events framework also apply.
sections.plainLanguage: Registration data can reveal where a user can be reached. Servers should check who may subscribe and protect the information they send.
